mission: Kael commits — 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.' The resonance trio is complete. The plan can execute.
why_now: Kael's decision — the final character commitment before the climax
conflict: The commitment is real — and so is the vulnerability. Kael has never voluntarily put himself at risk for others. The humor covers the magnitude of what he's doing.
turning_point: Kael's line: 'If this kills me, I want it on record that I volunteered. First time for everything.' Dry, self-aware, and the most important thing he's ever said. He's choosing. Not conscripted, not captured, not sealed. Choosing.
opening_hook: Kael walks back to the group. His stride is different — less careful, more deliberate. Ben watches him approach and knows the answer before he speaks.
closing_hook: The group moves toward the wound source — three Force-users and one non-Force-user, walking toward something unprecedented. Ben feels Sera's and Kael's Force presences beside him. Different. Complementary. Not yet a chord. But the notes are there.
emotional_trajectory: The commitment -> group relief and resolve -> the march toward the endgame

stakes.personal: Kael's arc payoff — chosen commitment, the antithesis of his Lie
stakes.interpersonal: The resonance trio formed — Ben, Sera, Kael. Three traditions, three wounds, one attempt.

setting: Veranthos — camp, then movement toward the valley
sensory_details: Kael's stride — deliberate, not careful; his voice delivering the line — dry, level, the humor covering something raw; three Force presences aligning — not harmonized yet but adjacent, complementary; the valley below, waiting
promises_paid: Kael's detachment breaks into chosen commitment (PP09)
notes: Kael's arc: new_truth_demonstrated. Kael/Veraine parallel resolution — same wound as Veraine, opposite choice. She chose destruction; he chooses participation. The 'first time for everything' line should be one of the book's most memorable.
